question: Select the functional group in five-carbon atom compound 'Pentanal'.
solution:
The correct answer is** Aldehyde**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

The functional group in pentanal is the aldehyde group, which is represented by the **-CHO **moiety.

 
• **Ketone**: Ketones have the general formula R(C=O)R', where R and R' can be alkyl or aryl groups. They are characterized by a carbonyl group (C=O) bonded to two other carbon atoms. Pentanal does not have a ketone functional group because it has a carbonyl group bonded to only one carbon atom.
 
• **Aldehyde**: Aldehydes are organic compounds containing a carbonyl group (C=O) bonded to at least one hydrogen atom, and the carbonyl carbon is always located at the terminal position of the carbon chain. Pentanal fits this description perfectly, as it has a carbonyl group (-CHO) bonded to one hydrogen atom and occupies the terminal position in a five-carbon chain.
 
• **Alcoho**l: Alcohols have the general formula R-OH, where R represents an alkyl or aryl group. They are characterized by the presence of a hydroxyl group (-OH) attached to a carbon atom. Pentanal does not have an alcohol functional group because it lacks the -OH group.
 
• ** Alkene**: Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons characterized by the presence of at least one carbon-carbon double bond (C=C). Pentanal does not contain any double bonds between carbon atoms, so it does not belong to the alkene functional group

 pentanal contains the aldehyde functional group (-CHO), making it an aldehyde compound.
